title: Finance Manager
description:
Danish Refugee Council, one of the world’s leading humanitarian NGOs, is currently looking for a highly qualified Finance Manager for our operations in Addis Ababa Country Office.

Instruction for applicants:
All applicants must upload a cover letter and an updated CV in English. Please ensure that your CV does not exceed three pages. Applications with CVs longer than the specified limit may not be considered


Overall purpose of the role 

This role has a country focus and ensures the financial health and stability of DRC ETH, foster strong donor relationships and support the organisational localisation efforts while ensuring compliance to DRC procedures and guidelines within the country. The role contributes to the development of country strategies, which are translated into action plans and day-to-day tasks. The role provides support and/or technical guidance to country operations while overseeing country Finance activities.

The Finance Manager is vested with powers to execute management policies and responsibilities to hire, suspend, layoff, dismiss or assign employees within the Finance department as necessary for the operations.

Your main duties and responsibilities will be:

Management & Leadership:

Within his/her management mandate, and in alignment with DRC’s leadership standards and policies, the position holder:


	Providing leadership and direction to a team, ensuring clarity of roles, expectations, and performance standards to achieve agreed goals and objectives.
	Exercising team budget oversight and decision-making authority where assigned.
	Leading or contributing to recruitment processes for staff within their team and implementing termination decisions in accordance with DRC’s two-step principle.
	Conducting and/or signing off on performance appraisals and ensuring regular, constructive feedback to support continuous improvement.
	Supporting the professional development of team members through coaching, capacity building, and development planning.
	Addressing poor performance and disciplinary issues, including handling Code of Conduct cases referred to management, in line with DRC policies and procedures.Is accountable for people management of direct reports, including hiring & firing, objective setting and priorities as per the strategic direction, probation, performance appraisal, development of staff, managing performance, including poor performance, etc.
	Is accountable for making sound decisions based on DRC policies, MOPs, standards, and the advice of technical experts in DRC.
	Accountable for making significant decisions on what the Finance team does: its purpose, functions and role, and for making commitments and decisions that require the expenditure of significant unit resources.
	Manages all finance related tasks within the country (Addis and field offices) - this includes but not limited to financial planning & analysis, cash flow management, financial risk management, budgeting & reporting, compliance and finance capacity building or teams and DRC implementing partners.
	Support the development and implementation of financial management capacity building of staff in the Country Finance team and provide support to the Area based Finance teams.
	Work to build the capacity of finance staff members throughout the program through frequent in-service training sessions and mentoring support.
	Ensure data protection and confidentiality in handling all financial information and organization documents


Financial Management and Planning 


	Oversee the finance department for the entire operation, providing training and oversight to country office finance staff as well as advising and ensuring adequate support to area office finance staff.
	In close cooperation with Managers and AMs, reinforce existing procedures and systems for financial management and control in compliance with guidelines of DRC’s Operations Handbook, internal guidelines and donor requirements.
	Support timely delivery of quality financial reports to donors and internal reports to colleagues and HQ.
	Ensure compliance with relevant country statutory and other financial obligations such as tax, levies and statutory returns.
	Monthly/weekly financial briefings to Head of Support Services
	Ensure Finance team preparation and active participation in monthly Budget Follow Up reviews and in monthly/quarterly Project Monitoring Meeting (financial aspects) to discuss key variances, reasons for these, and any remedial action that is required.
	Ensure thorough and effective budgetary control in the country programs.
	Liaise with relevant Managers and budget holders on key financial issues for all programs in the country, including co-funding, financial reporting, key variances, and recommend and support any remedial action required, reporting major issues to the Head of Support Services for action.
	Collecting cash forecasts from all Programme Managers and requesting funds in a timely manner.

title: Support Service Team Leader
description:
Support Service Team Leader 

 

The Danish Refugee Council (DRC), one of the world’s leading NGOs, with a focus on responding to displacement, have been registered in Sudan since 2004, delivering life-saving programming in protection, emergency response, shelter, food security and livelihoods, disaster risk reduction, camp management, and humanitarian mine action. DRC has implemented projects in Central Darfur, South Kordofan, Gedaref, Port Sudan, and White Nile. Sudan hosts one of the largest displaced populations in Africa, with over 3.7 million internally displaced people and over 1.1 million refugees from South Sudan, Ethiopia, Eritrea, Central African Republic, Chad, Yemen and Syria. Against a background of political crisis, Sudan faces economic and social turmoil, with sharp increases in food and energy costs, further exacerbated by disease outbreaks and ongoing conflict.

 

POSITION PROFILE

The purpose of the Support Services Team Leader is to coordinate the support functions at Area Office. Responsibilities encompass all support activities for the DRC Gedaref office. This role has an area focus and ensures compliance with DRC procedures and guidelines within the area office. The role contributes to the development of area strategies, which are translated into action plans and day-to-day tasks. The role provides support and/or technical guidance to all operations in the area of responsibility.

 

Overall purpose of the role:


	Line management of support staff such as Finance, HR & Admin and Supply Chain & Logistics
	Member of the Area Management Team
	Compliance with and adherence to DRC policies, guidance, and operations handbooks and donor/auditor requirements
	Provide operational support to the Area Plan of Action, and coordinate and align operational support with program plans at Area level
	Responsible for ensuring quality support to project implementation
	Facilitate, Area Support Budget, including support cost, under the supervision of the AM.
	Ensure effective budgetary control and adherence to DRC and donor policies and procedures
	Responsible for developing regular reports at the area level to Country Office and AM
	Responsible for implementation of technical SOPs, guidelines and tools in Area (HR, Logistic/ICT and Finance)
	Facilitate trainings for programme staff on finance, logistics and HR procedures
	Responsible for technical capacity building of support staff (HR, Logistic/ICT and Finance)
	Ensure close coordination and maintain excellent working relationships with local authorities and relevant stakeholders.


Support in ensuring safety and security of DRC staff, premises and assets in the operational areas.

 

DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES

Responsibilities:

These responsibilities shall be adapted to the particularities of the job location and context, phase of operation, strategic focus and type of programme intervention. This section shall be revised whenever the context changes significantly.


	Advise and support Project Managers and Support Staff in the implementation of support-related SOPs.
	Ensure strong coordination with County Office support departments and act as the focal point for coordination of support departments between the Country Office and the Area Office.
	Contribute to strengthen the area-level implementation through the dissemination and monitoring of relevant SOPs and procedures.
	Oversee implementation of identified risk mitigation measures, including compliance spot checks in line with anti–corruption risk mapping
	Under the country office and AM’s guidance, ensure compliance with the Securing Supporting Documentation (SSD) SOP as well as the existing Country Office Data Management System.
	Responsible for support resource allocation on the area level in line with the Master Budget and available project budgets.
	Ensure that thorough and effective budgetary control is in place, and ensure accountability and donor compliance in all financial documentation
	In line with guidelines and under supervision of AM, coordinate and align operational support with program plans at Area level, ensuring procurement plans, HR plans and spending plans for each project are in place.
	Oversee HR procedures based on the global people policy, including recruitment, development, performance, contracts, well-being and people planning.
	Ensure that support services are fit for purpose to meet program needs.
	Be the focal point for the compliance self-check and internal audits.


 

 

SKILLS AND EXPERIENCES


	Minimum 5 years of relevant work experience and 2 years at a management level



	Sound knowledge of cost planning, budgeting, and financial reporting
	Experience in management of HR and administrative teams
	Good knowledge of procurement procedures of INGOs
	Experience of working on donor-funded projects
	Full professional proficiency in English and Arabic


EDUCATIONAL QUALIFICATIONS


	Bachelor’s degree in supply chain, Logistics, Procurement, Finance, Accounting, HR,
